clue.text: Sort of compound established by gangster and goddess

parts.note: Al Capone, the Chicago gangster, gives his first name
Kali is the Hindu goddess of destruction

explanation.surface: A mobster and a deity found some kind of business compound together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compound' tempts as a walled enclosure, but here it is a chemical one.
explanation.definitionFit: Alkalis are a class of chemical substance, bases that dissolve in water.

clue.text: Sailor's in the drink

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor; with the 's it gives ABS
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A seaman has fallen overboard into the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The drink' is slang for the sea, which is the surface picture; split differently, the clue spells out the answer, with 'drink' alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinthe is a strong anise-flavoured spirit, the 'green fairy'.

clue.text: Ruler goes round always keeping dry in town

indicators.note: the ruler's word is placed around everything else, enclosing it

parts.note: a king is a ruler

indicators.note: the word for always holds the word for dry inside itself

parts.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always
TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol

explanation.surface: A monarch on tour stays sober throughout his visit to a town.
explanation.walkthrough: KETTERING is a town in Northamptonshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Kettering is a market town in the English Midlands.

clue.text: Space between lines for principal actor

definitions.meaning: in printing, strips of metal were used to space out lines of type, and that spacing is named after the metal
the star role, or the actor playing it

explanation.definitionFit: In typesetting this metal strip widened line spacing; in theatre it names the starring role or performer.

clue.text: Berate a couple of females interrupting platform

indicators.note: the middle pieces break into the word for berate, splitting it

parts.note: to berate is to scold
F is the abbreviation for female; two of them give FF

explanation.surface: Two women heckle someone who is ranting from a stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A scaffold is a raised wooden platform, as used for builders or executions.

clue.text: Tin with mushy peas for starters

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: mushy peas are mashed up, so the letters of peas are mashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A tin of mushy peas served as the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: Mushy peas are a British side dish of mashed marrowfat peas, often eaten with fish and chips.
explanation.definitionFit: Canapés are small savoury bites served before a meal, as appetisers.

clue.text: A mare falls badly? Nothing really to worry about

indicators.note: something going badly is in disarray, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A horse stumbles at a fence, but it turns out to be nothing serious.
explanation.definitionFit: A false alarm is a warning of danger that proves groundless.

clue.text: African organisation on island offering a haven

parts.note: the OAS was the Organisation armée secrète, a paramilitary group in French Algeria

explanation.surface: An African body based on an island provides a refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is a fertile spot in a desert, and figuratively any place of refuge.

clue.text: Bold and lovable person losing heart

indicators.note: the central letter of the word for a lovable person is dropped

parts.note: a darling is a lovable person

explanation.surface: A sweetheart who loses heart must still be brave.
explanation.walkthrough: DARLING loses its middle letter L.
explanation.definitionFit: Daring means bold or audacious.

clue.text: One learner into male fashion, being a poet

indicators.note: the first pair of pieces goes inside the male-and-fashion pair

parts.note: ton means fashion or style, as in 'the ton' of high society
I is the Roman numeral for one
L is for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A trainee getting into men's fashion has a poetic streak.
explanation.definitionFit: John Milton was the English poet who wrote Paradise Lost.

clue.text: Travelling to Tunisia for a job

indicators.note: the letters of 'to Tunisia' move about, travelling into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is relocating to North Africa for work.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation is a post or position of employment, as in 'situations vacant'.

clue.text: One may need a lot of resolve to make a comeback

definitions.text: One may need a lot of resolve to make a comeback

indicators.note: coming back means the remaining letters run in reverse order
most of the word resolve is used, its last two letters dropped

explanation.surface: Someone defeated needs great determination to recover.
explanation.walkthrough: RESOL, most of 'resolve', is turned round. The whole clue also describes the answer: a beaten competitor needs grit to fight back.
explanation.definitionFit: A defeated competitor is the one needing determination to recover.

clue.text: Want someone to look after the Gateshead Gazette, say?

parts.note: Gateshead is in the North East of England, NE
an editor, ED, looks after a newspaper

explanation.surface: A local newspaper is advertising for a person to run it.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gateshead Gazette, say, is a paper in the North East; its editor would be an NE ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To want something is to require it, a synonym.

clue.text: Engineer making a bit of progress when joined by female and boy

parts.note: a step is a small advance
a hen is a female bird
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: An engineer advances when a woman and a lad join the team.
explanation.walkthrough: George and Robert Stephenson were pioneering British railway engineers (the Rocket locomotive).
explanation.definitionFit: George Stephenson was the railway pioneer who built early steam locomotives.

clue.text: Chemist once giving a drug to the man-big name in films

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis
he refers to the man
Cary Grant was a Hollywood star

explanation.surface: A pharmacist once supplied narcotics to a famous movie actor.
explanation.definitionFit: An apothecary was an old-time pharmacist who prepared and sold medicines.

clue.text: Car may have trouble negotiating this — it's stuck in a lock

definitions.text: Car may have trouble negotiating this
definitions.meaning: a very sharp U-shaped bend on a road is hard to drive round
a pin pushed into a lock of hair holds it in place

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a tight road bend and a U-shaped clip for keeping hair in place.

clue.text: Choose religious group to accommodate the French or the Spanish

indicators.note: the religious group's word takes the article inside itself

parts.note: a sect is a religious group
le is French for the and el is Spanish for the; either fits, as the two letters can go in both ways

explanation.surface: Pick a church that will make room for French or Spanish members.
explanation.definitionFit: To select is to pick out from a group.

clue.text: A person in a group in court from a place in Normandy

indicators.note: the pair of pieces goes inside the abbreviation for court

parts.note: a member is someone belonging to a group

explanation.surface: Someone in a gang appears in a courtroom having come from northern France.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads like a description of a person; it describes a cheese named after its village.
explanation.definitionFit: Camembert, the soft cheese, comes from the Normandy village of that name.

clue.text: Terribly sad now about 5-0? That's right!

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go round the score
something done terribly is messed up, so the letters of 'sad now' are scrambled

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five and O is nought

explanation.surface: Someone is upset at a 5-0 result, then exclaims it was correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terribly' scrambles SAD NOW into ADWSON, and 'about' wraps that round VO. An advowson is a right, the exclamation's 'right' being a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An advowson is the legal entitlement in English church law to nominate a parish priest.

clue.text: A place where there was to be no telling by a girl

parts.words: place where there was to be no telling
parts.note: in the Bible David laments 'Tell it not in Gath', a Philistine city

explanation.surface: A girl was in a place where secrets had to be kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha is a girl's name, as of the novelist Agatha Christie.

clue.text: A revolutionary capturing leader of Athens, an old Greek

indicators.note: the revolutionary's name holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Marxist revolutionary

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A rebel seizes the head of an ancient Greek city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Achaeans were Homer's name for the ancient Greeks.

clue.text: Like a style of selling that won't be seen as pointless?

definitions.meaning: a scheme in which each recruit signs up more sellers below them, widening at the base

definitions.text: that won't be seen as pointless?
definitions.meaning: a solid figure tapering to a point at the top is obviously not pointless

explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a tiered sales scheme and names a solid with a pointed apex.

clue.text: Still cold when wrapped in cloth

indicators.note: the letter for cold is enclosed by the word for cloth

parts.note: plaid is a tartan cloth
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Keeping warm and motionless while bundled up in a blanket.
explanation.definitionFit: Placid and still both mean calm and undisturbed.

clue.text: Famously wet doctor providing nurture

definitions.meaning: in the nursery rhyme, Doctor ... went to Gloucester in a shower of rain and stepped in a puddle
to bring up a child not one's own, caring for it

explanation.definitionFit: The nursery-rhyme doctor shares his name with the verb for raising a child as a guardian.

clue.text: Naughty phone cheat avoiding lots of expense

indicators.note: naughty behaviour is disorderly, so the letters of 'phone cheat' are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dishonest caller dodges paying for his calls.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something this way means doing it cheaply, spending little.

clue.text: Fish objectionable person hauled up on lake

indicators.note: in a down clue, hauling up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a wart is slang for an unpleasant person

explanation.surface: An angler pulls an unpleasant character out of the water.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed below, so the lake's letter goes after the upturned word; 'hauled up' fits the fishing picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To trawl is to fish by dragging a net behind a boat.

clue.text: University doctor meeting old boss

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: An academic medic has a meeting with a former employer.
explanation.definitionFit: An umbo is the raised central knob on a shield, also called a boss.

clue.text: River giving smell by the sound of it

indicators.note: the word for smell is said aloud to give the spelling entered

parts.note: an odour is a smell

explanation.surface: A river is said to give off a smell.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oder is a central European river forming part of the German-Polish border.

clue.text: Bejewelled item? It's back to front on a royal body!

indicators.note: the word it is turned round

parts.note: the clue word It, with 's read as 'is'
RA is the Royal Academy

explanation.surface: A crown worn the wrong way round at a royal gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' looks like 'it is', but the 's is only the possessive link; RA, the Royal Academy, is a standard crossword royal body.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled crown-like ornament worn on the head.

clue.text: Bad people may be reviled so

indicators.note: suggests that 'reviled so' could be rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: Wicked folk might be condemned like this.
explanation.definitionFit: Evildoers are wrongdoers, people who commit wicked acts.

clue.text: Call for friend to join in motor sport

indicators.note: the friend's word joins in, entering the word for call

parts.note: to ring is to call on the phone
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: Ringing a mate to come along to a car race.
explanation.definitionFit: Rallying is a form of motor racing on public or off-road stages.

clue.text: Dish makin 'an unpleasant sound?

indicators.note: makin', with its dropped G, shows the final G being dropped from the next word

parts.note: a grating is a harsh, unpleasant sound

explanation.surface: A dish that makes a screeching noise.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in makin' marks a dropped G, so GRATING loses its last letter too.
explanation.definitionFit: A gratin is a dish topped with browned breadcrumbs or cheese.
